subject: Replace hardcoded split dates with dynamic proportional cutoffs
description:
Brian, 2026-08-12: "this should not even be a hardcoded date cutoff, it should follow dynamic sorted positional (percentage) cutoff following the best practice of train, val, test splits, so it should be dynamic by nature which it is not."

Correct, and MEASURED -- the hardcoded defaults have silently drifted into a bad split.

_shared_modules/engineer_features.py:38-39 pins DEFAULT_TRAIN_END=(2025,2) and DEFAULT_VAL_END=(2025,8); apply_split() (line 407) labels rows against those fixed Timestamps.

ACTUAL SPLIT ON THE FRESH EXTRACT (2026-07):
  CSD          46 periods  29/6/11  = 63/13/24
  Danskvand    41 periods  24/6/11  = 59/15/27
  Energidrikke 43 periods  26/6/11  = 60/14/26
  RTD          41 periods  24/6/11  = 59/15/27

Test is 24-27%, nearly DOUBLE the intended ~15%; training starved at 59-63%. Cause: fixed cutoffs mean every newly-arrived month falls into  by default. The 2026-08-12 re-pull added 2-4 months straight to test.

THREE PROBLEMS:
1. Silent drift -- nothing errors; ratio degrades on every refresh; results not comparable between runs.
2. Cross-category incomparability -- SRQ1 claims ranking "on identical data", but CSD trains on 63% and RTD on 59% purely from differing panel starts. Part of any ranking difference is split artifact.
3. Undersized training set exactly where panel depth is already the binding constraint.

FIX: compute cutoffs from PROPORTIONS against each category own sorted period list.
  - Parameters train_frac / val_frac (e.g. 0.70 / 0.15), not dates.
  - Sort unique dates, slice positionally, derive cutoff dates from slice boundaries.
  - Chronological order preserved -- no shuffling, no leakage. Standard temporal-split practice.
  - Self-corrects on refresh; no constant to maintain.
  - Keep the date-tuple form as an OVERRIDE for reproducing a specific historical split.

WATCH: apply_split runs on the CALENDAR-FILLED frame where every brand shares the same date range, so a global positional cutoff is well-defined. Verify that holds -- if coverage differs, compute on the global sorted date axis, not per brand.

ALSO: record the resulting split (dates + counts) in the output artifact so any published result states the exact window used.

Verify: all four categories land within ~1 period of target ratio; boundaries reported per category; re-running after a future refresh preserves the ratio rather than growing test.
activeForm: Replacing hardcoded split with proportional cutoffs
